title: Declarative annotation layer, offscreen tiling, and keyboard-first ARIA navigation for time-series charts
creator: Aisha Bennett
description:
Problem: our existing time-series charts struggle with three coupled issues: (1) dense datasets cause DOM/paint bottlenecks for long time ranges, (2) legend and tooltip keyboard interactions are inconsistent across themes and density modes, and (3) annotation editing/authoring is tightly coupled to runtime rendering so it's difficult to preview or reuse semantic groups.

This ticket proposes a cohesive design solution consisting of: a) a declarative annotation layer (annotation model + UI controls) so designers and users can author semantic groups (events, thresholds, spans) independently of the rendering pipeline; b) offscreen tiling / differential hydration where high-density regions are pre-rendered to an offscreen canvas and streamed into the viewport to reduce main-thread layout thrash; and c) a keyboard-first ARIA navigation pattern for legends + tooltip focus that uses a roving focus model and a single ARIA live summary region that synthesizes concise narrative summaries (one-line per series or group) instead of dumping raw data points to screen readers.

Goals: reduce peak frame work in long-range views, provide keyboard-first accessible exploration of legends and annotations, and enable designers to surface semantic annotation sets as tokens in the design system for reuse across charts and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: Design spec with Figma components for: annotation authoring panel, semantic group chips, compact/expanded legend states, and keyboard-first focus flows
Annotated interaction flows showing roving focus (left/right legend navigation; enter -> open tooltip; esc -> close) and aria live summary examples for screen readers
Performance playbook describing offscreen tiling thresholds (e.g., >10k samples or >5 series in 10s viewport) and fallback behavior when GPU acceleration is unavailable
Tokens defined for chart density modes (compact, default, immersive): spacing, tokenized stroke widths, marker scales, and summary verbosity mapping
Engineering prototype PR linked and basic bench results demonstrating >35% reduction in main-thread time on 60s-range synthetic traces
Usability sign-off from Accessibility reviewer and Product Designer with checklist items completed
comments: 2026-03-07 Aisha Bennett: Scoped initial problem statement and sketched three options in Figma — (A) inline annotation layer, (B) declarative side-panel + tokens, (C) server-side pre-baked tiles. Recommend B + client-side offscreen tiling hybrid.
2026-03-08 Luca Moreno: Reviewed feasibility with Eng (ENG-90214). Eng asked for explicit thresholds and a simple fallback (canvas -> svg) for older browsers. Added perf acceptance criteria.

2026-03-09 Accessibility review (J. Park): Agreed with roving focus approach; asked for concrete aria-live phrasing examples and a short mode for screen readers in compact charts. Action: add examples to spec.
2026-03-10 Product feedback (M. Alvarez): Likes annotation tokenization for reuse across dashboards; requested quicksave presets for customer support workflows. Added to follow-up backlog.

2026-03-11 Engineering update (ENG-90622): Prototype PR shows 38% main-thread reduction in synthetic load test but requires explicit invalidation when annotations toggle. Added a microtask debounce to annotation edits.

2026-03-12 Aisha Bennett: Pushed updated Figma with keyboard flow overlays and aria sample copy. Requesting design review from Y. Singh and accessibility final check before handing to Eng for integration sprint.
